newsitem.title: CANADA: Crowd blocks media bus in Chretien election tour.
newsitem.headline: Crowd blocks media bus in Chretien election tour.

text.p: An angry crowd complaining of unemployment and a lack of fish blocked a media bus on Friday that was planning to cover a campaign event by Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.

Shouting "We want jobs," the approximately 300 milled around the bus, breaking its windscreen wipers and preventing it from moving, Reuters photographer Peter Jones reported. Chretien's bus was to have arrived 45 minutes later but appeared to be holding back until the situation cleared up.

The media bus was attacked about nine miles (14 km) away from the site of a new oil platform that Chretien was to inaugurate on Friday as part of the C$5.8 billion ($4.2 billion U.S.) Hibernia oil project, scheduled to start producing in late 1997.
It has been one of the economic hopes for Newfoundland, Canada's poorest province where fishermen face depleted stocks and unemployment runs at 19.1 percent.

Buzz Hargrove, president of the Canadian Auto Workers union, was milling through the crowd, which carried signs decrying the Liberal federal government's tough fishing restrictions: "Empty nets, empty promises."
The demonstration came as the federal agency Statistics Canada revealed that the country's unemployment rate jumped to 9.6 percent in April from 9.3 percent.
